reason: The passage explicitly depicts God threatening to strike the people with pestilence and disinherit them (אַכֶּנּוּ בַדֶּבֶר וְאוֹרִשֶׁנּוּ), while declaring He will make Moses into a nation 'greater and mightier' (לְגוֹי־ גָּדוֹל וְעָצוּם מִמֶּנּוּ). This demonstrates that Yahweh does not consider Himself bound by unconditional loyalty to the Israelites, and is explicitly considering their replacement with a new people formed from Moses. The conditional nature of the covenant is evident: the people's faithlessness and rejection of God's signs triggers this threat of disinheritance and replacement.
